- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.27) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral/negative.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.11) over 3+ days, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion.  
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed; apply a 2–5% downward bias for first 5–7 days if sentiment is volatile.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often misses the rebound; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% in the 2nd–3rd day of sentiment shift.  
- Model underestimates when sentiment is neutral (0.00) and recent price is falling; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
